item.title: 🟠 Ignite 2026: What's new in Microsoft Defender & Sentinel
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

At Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re announcing new innovations across Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Sentinel that bring security operations and threat protection closer together, help organizations get ahead of attacks, secure AI agents and strengthen protection across critical workloads.

  • The foundation for agentic security: Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender now includes the full breadth of SIEM capabilities and 90-days of built-in Defender data.
  • Protection before the patch: Vulnerability shielding in Defender autonomously protects exposed systems before and during active attacks, giving security teams more time to deploy permanent patches to vulnerabilities.
  • Protect AI agents wherever they run: Manage security posture for third-party agent platforms, prevent device code phishing and extend runtime protection for local AI agents on Windows.
  • Protect people where they work: Extend defenses against browser-based attacks, malicious QR codes in Teams, and synthetic media threats.

Together, these innovations build on a shared foundation of signals, actuators, and coordinated response to help security teams move faster and stop attacks before they spread.

The foundation for agentic security

ISOC now includes the full breadth of SIEM capabilities and 90 days of built-in retention…

Source: Microsoft 365 Defender Blog  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 2d

item.title: 🟠 Ignite 2026: What’s new in endpoint security
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

As more work happens in the browser, the browser has become a prime target for attackers. A fake CAPTCHA or a convincing error message persuades users to take an action that seems harmless, like running a command or approving a request. In these attacks, the user unknowingly carries the threat from the browser to the operating system. Once that happens, the attacker can install malware, steal credentials, or establish a foothold on the device.

This sequence creates a practical challenge for defenders. Preventing breach at the time of execution is key, and at the same time security teams need confidence that protection is deployed, communicating, current, and functioning across all endpoints in the environment.

At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Microsoft Defender is introducing protection designed to block some of the most prevalent browser-based attacks, and new capabilities to better and more easily manage the endpoint estate itself.

Together, these updates connect two responsibilities that security teams often manage separately: stopping an attack when it becomes executable and continuously verifying that the protection layer is ready to respond.

item.title: 🔴 Vulnerability shielding: Protect the time before the patch
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.

AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery for defenders and attackers alike. An attacker can now turn a vulnerability into a working exploit within hours, but patching can’t keep pace. Our data shows that 38% of critical Patch Tuesday exposures remain unpatched for more than five days, and attackers operate in the gap between exposure and remediation.

To keep up, organizations need protection that moves as fast as critical vulnerabilities are discovered, without forcing rushed patches or disrupting the business. That’s why today we’re excited to introduce vulnerability shielding in Microsoft Defender, in preview:

Vulnerability shielding applies targeted, temporary protection to vulnerable systems in the gap between exposure and remediation, buying defenders time before they can apply a permanent patch. This AI-based capability reasons over the latest threat intelligence and each organization’s unique environment to choose the narrowest effective protection. Vulnerability shielding operates at two critical moments:

  • Proactively limit exposure: The Risk Reduction Agent in Microsoft Perception as part of the Reduce exposure risk playbook creates a tailored plan for shielding vulnerabilities when patching is not immediately available or possible. Shields are time bound, reversible, choose the path of minimal business disruption,…
